open_points.subject: A17 configuration and credential file opening
open_points.text: “the last component for reading with `O_NONBLOCK` as well, so a component that is no regular file is refused by the checks rather than waited on”
open_points.question: Is opening the final component required never to block before its regular-file check, or is merely supplying `O_NONBLOCK` sufficient even though Linux does not guarantee nonblocking open behavior for every device or file-system object?
options: The open must never block; specify an additional mechanism that guarantees this before opening for reading.
The kernel only has to pass `O_NONBLOCK`; a Linux object whose open still blocks is permitted to block.
Such objects or file systems are unsupported under A20, and the kernel may block or otherwise behave undefined there.
open_points.default_guess: Pass `O_NONBLOCK`, then check the opened descriptor, treating any Linux object that ignores the flag as unsupported.
